findings.statement: Building the key index across threads speeds up the build
findings.detail: sort plus encode 0.0490s parallel against 0.0744s sequential (sequential vs parallel: greater 1.518x (p=0.0051, rel_iqr 19.7%/11.7%)). Both halves are threaded now: the sort splits and merges, and the record loop splits because is a prefix sum, so a range of keys owns a contiguous range of record bytes and its directory entries are  -- disjoint by construction, no atomics

findings.statement: That speed-up is visible in the load it is part of
findings.detail: 1074281 ops/s parallel against 1063053 sequential (parallel vs sequential: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.011, p=0.6761) -- within noise, not a result). f31 put the ceiling at 7% for the sort alone before this was written, which is the point of measuring it: a change whose best case is single digits has to clear the noise of the thing it is embedded in, and that is a different question from whether the sort got faster

notes: both arms interleaved; the only difference is Options::parallel_index
